item: storage_events.record's trim loops keep their back-edge inside the lock (R163)
refs: R163; hunk pair from Q, remade on this tree; PR #1429
summary: storage_events.record is called by the write gate's hold bookkeeping (writer._note_hold_end, _note_long_hold) and the storage guard on whichever thread held the gate, so a CLI's main thread reaches it (a write lock's release records a gate hold) and the event-loop exemption (R165) does not cover it. Its keep-rule drop (the LONGEST trim), the oldest-first eviction loop and the comprehensions inside them left their back-edges outside the with on CPython 3.13, so a Ctrl-C landing there left _LOCK owned. Three helpers (_forget_open_of, _forget_unkept, _evict_one) hold the comprehensions and the eviction, and the loop is while True with the bound test first. Same trimming, same order, same open-key forgetting. Q wrote the pair on this tree; the code and its new test file go in one commit. The dis test (Q's _uncovered_loop_heads) is red on the old code; three behaviour tests pin that an open run is not pushed out, that an evicted event forgets its open key, and that the LONGEST drop forgets the keys of what it drops.
